symptoms: A stage retries and the task set reports an executor that stopped answering
The failure repeats on different executors as the stage is retried
Other stages of the same run complete normally
likely_causes: The executor process died -- memory outside the heap, or the container manager killed it
The executor was removed by dynamic allocation while a task was still assigned to it
The node hosting the executor was reclaimed, which is the expected behaviour on interruptible capacity
diagnostic_steps: Read the reason the event log records for the loss: a killed container, an exit code and a decommission are three different stories under the same message
Compare how many executors were lost against how many the run had: losing one of forty is not the same event as losing most of them
Read whether the stage that failed is the same one every time, which separates a data-shaped cause from an infrastructure-shaped one
fixes: Treat the memory outside the heap when the reason is a killed container -- it is a different budget from the heap
Read the purchasing option of the capacity when losses are spread and the reason is decommission: interruptible capacity being reclaimed is not a defect
Reduce the data a single task carries when the same stage dies repeatedly
unsafe_fixes: Raising the number of task retries so the run finishes: it hides the loss and pays for it in wall clock every time
Raising executor memory before reading the reason -- a decommissioned node does not care how much memory the executor had
verification: Re-run and compare the number of executors lost against the previous run, over the same input volume. A run that completes with the same number of losses did not fix the cause
rollback: Revert the capacity or memory change. If the treatment changed data distribution, the output has to be compared before the previous version is discarded
